name: Singapore
tagline: Two global top-20 universities four hours from Dhaka
summary: Singapore hosts NUS and NTU, both inside the QS world top 20, taught entirely in English and reachable in a four-hour direct flight from Dhaka. Fees are high by Asian standards but the MOE Tuition Grant cuts them sharply in exchange for a three-year work commitment in Singapore after graduation.
why_study: English-medium instruction throughout|two universities in the global top 20|the MOE Tuition Grant materially reduces published fees in return for a service obligation|a short direct flight and a large South Asian community
visa_summary: Student's Pass issued by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority after the institution registers the applicant through the SOLAR system. Apply once an offer is accepted.
work_rights: Full-time students at approved institutions may work up to 16 hours per week during term and without restriction during vacation.
post_study_work: Graduates may apply for a Long-Term Visit Pass to remain and seek employment; holders of the MOE Tuition Grant are bound to work for a Singapore-registered employer for three years.

name: Saudi Arabia
tagline: Fully funded government scholarships across 27+ public universities
summary: The Saudi Ministry of Education runs a single national scholarship portal covering more than 27 public universities. Awards typically include full tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, annual flights and health insurance, which makes Saudi Arabia one of the few destinations where a strong applicant can study at close to zero cost.
why_study: One unified, free government application covering 27+ universities|packages that routinely cover tuition, housing, stipend and flights|five institutions in the QS world top 500|strong provision in engineering, petroleum, medicine and Islamic studies
visa_summary: Educational visa arranged after a scholarship or admission offer is issued; scholarship students are processed through the Ministry of Education platform.
work_rights: Work rights are limited and tied to the terms of the scholarship or sponsoring university; students should confirm with their institution before accepting outside work.
post_study_work: Pathways to work residency exist under Vision 2030 reforms but are not automatic; confirm current rules with the sponsoring university.

name: Spain
tagline: Regulated public tuition and a 24-month post-study job search permit
summary: Spanish public universities charge regulated per-credit rates set by each autonomous community, so the same degree costs very different amounts in Madrid than in Valencia or Andalusia. Non-EU undergraduates typically pay more in Madrid and Catalonia and the same as EU students in several other regions.
why_study: Public tuition regulated by region rather than set by the institution|a growing English-taught catalogue|three universities in the QS world top 200|a 24-month post-study permit to look for work
visa_summary: Long-stay student visa applied for at the Spanish consulate once an admission letter is issued, converted to a TIE residence card after arrival.
work_rights: Students may work up to 30 hours per week with a valid study authorisation, provided it does not interfere with study.
post_study_work: A 24-month residence permit to search for work or start a business is available to graduates of Spanish institutions.

name: Türkiye
summary: Türkiye's official Study in Türkiye portal lists 208 universities offering close to 45,000 degree programmes, with a dedicated entrance examination for international candidates (TR-YÖS) held across dozens of countries. Public university fees are low and a large share of programmes are taught in English.
why_study: 208 universities and roughly 45,000 programmes|TR-YÖS entrance examination run in 78 centres across 52 countries|low public-university fees|direct flights and an established Bangladeshi student community
visa_summary: Student visa applied for at a Turkish mission after acceptance, followed by a residence permit application within the first month after arrival.
work_rights: Work rights depend on degree level and institution type; undergraduates generally require a work permit and may work only after the first year.
post_study_work: Graduates may apply for a short-term residence permit and transition to a work permit once employed.

name: Austria
tagline: A flat statutory tuition fee of EUR 726.72 per semester at public universities
summary: Austria charges non-EU students a tuition fee fixed in law at EUR 726.72 per semester at its public universities, the same figure regardless of subject, city or institution, plus a small students' union fee. Twenty-three public universities sit alongside universities of applied sciences and private institutions.
why_study: A statutory, predictable fee of EUR 726.72 per semester at every public university|23 public universities plus applied-sciences institutions|Vienna repeatedly ranked among the world's most liveable cities|strong German-taught provision with a widening English-taught master's catalogue
visa_summary: Residence permit for students applied for before travel at an Austrian representative authority, with proof of admission and sufficient funds.
work_rights: Students may work alongside study subject to permit conditions, commonly cited at around 20 hours per week.
post_study_work: A 12-month residence permit to seek employment is available to graduates of Austrian institutions.
